newsitem.title: UK: Branson team to make round-world attempt on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Branson team to make round-world attempt on Tuesday.

text.p: Flamboyant British businessman Richard Branson plans to set off on Tuesday on his bid to make the first round-the-world trip by balloon, his spokeswoman said on Sunday.
Branson, and his two co-pilots, plan to start the trip from a Marrakesh military base at dawn on Tuesday if the weather remains good, spokeswoman Jackie McQuillan said.

"The plan is for the balloon to go up on Tuesday or Wednesday at the latest. The weather is forming perfectly globally for early next week. We will be up and ready by dawn on Tuesday. The team is all very excited," she said.
Branson, who has been on a skiing holiday in Europe with his family, was flying to Morocco from Zurich.

The flight is estimated to take between 14 and 21 days and should end in Branson's home town of Oxford in England. Branson, the 45-year-old boss of the Virgin group of companies, was thwarted last January by constant bad weather from making the attempt in a 900,000 cu ft (25,500 cu m) balloon.
At the time, he called the attempt "a mad adventure".
A new, bigger Virgin Global Challenger, a helium and hot air balloon of 1.1 million cu ft (31,100 cu m), was brought to Morocco in November.

Branson and team members Per Linstrand and Rory McCarthy spent three days training in the new balloon in December and have been waiting since for ideal weather in Morocco to take them straight into the southerly sub-tropical jet stream.
From Morocco the balloon should fly across North Africa, Saudi Arabia and India, descending to the South China Sea and then across the Pacific Ocean.
It should cross the United States somewhere between San Francisco and Seattle before arriving in England.

The balloon flight is the latest in a series of record-breaking attempts that have indulged Branson's taste for adventure while earning publicity for his companies, which include Virgin Atlantic Airways, a radio station, a chain of superstores, a cinema chain and ventures in cola and vodka.
Branson and Lindstrand came close to death twice on previous record-breaking balloon flights in 1987 and 1991.
